What actually made her famous was social media. Under the name Courtney Taylor she

In 2020 she made about $900,000 Schmuelney fans. In 2021 more than 1.8 million.
They started dating in November 2020. They were together a little under two years.
One more thing about her because it comes up later. Rolling Stone reported she had one DUI

Police put it in the warrant this way. Multiple incidents of domestic violence from both sides

And then there is the video. On February 21 2022 at about 8,030 at night a camera in the

Prosecutors released that video at a news conference. It is the single most seen piece

If you only ever see one piece of this case that is the one you will see and it is very hard to

On April 1 they got back together and he moved back in. That same night police were called to

I have not always been a victim but like right now I am the victim in this situation.
One account says she had bruises on her arms and legs. The officers noted she appeared intoxicated.
Nobody was arrested. Stop on that for a second because April 1 is the whole case in miniature.
Inside one police visit you have a woman saying she is being stalked and asking about a

Everybody in this story had a version and the versions did not fit together and nobody had to

She was not arrested. At the time the preliminary read was that this looked like

I will tell you the sequence. A man was stabbed to death. The woman who did it went home that

There is one more fact in that stretch worth knowing. The Miami police department's own
early statement said the preliminary investigation determined that both Obam Selle and the female
had been involved in a physical altercation. That is how it was framed at first as a fight.
Rundle's office then opened a review that ran four months and Miami police went back
through it with the state attorney's office obtaining several warrants and subpoenas,
pulling cell phone extraction data, recorded statements, 911 calls and records,
and taking information from law enforcement agencies in other states.
What changed was the science. Clennie's account to police was that Obam Selle shoved her against
the wall by her neck, threw her to the ground and that she picked up a kitchen knife and threw
it at him for more than 10 feet away. A thrown knife. She said she never meant to kill him.
The Miami day chief medical examiner Kenneth Hutchins found that the cause of death was a stab

side of his chest. That wound explains what officers found in that apartment, the two
large pools in the blood at different levels, and it explains what you can hear in the 911
call. A wound like that at that angle in that depth does not come from a knife thrown across a room.
That was the medical examiner's conclusion and it is the hinge the whole case turned on.
There was a second problem. Clennie said he had choked her and thrown her down.
The Miami police chief, Manuel Morales, put it bluntly, there was no physical evidence to
suggest she was actually harmed in any way on the day of the incident. No bruises consistent
with choking. She never claimed he had a weapon. And in her own recorded statement,
after giving accounts that investigators called inconsistent, Clennie said this,
I don't know. I really don't know if this was justified at all.
There was one more thing in that warrant. At 5.25 that evening, 28 minutes after the 911 call,
a text arrived on Clennie's phone from mom. It mentioned self-defense and it advised her not
to say anything to investigators without an attorney. There is a wrinkle in what her
mother told police. In her own recorded statement to investigators that day,
she rejected the idea that she and her daughter had been discussing the fight while it was going on.
She heard it happen. She told him she was not part of it. On the morning of August 10, 2022,
officers from the Hawaii police department and United States Marshals arrested Courtney Clennie
on Hawaii Island on a Florida warrant for second-degree murder with a deadly weapon. She was 26.
Her attorney said he was completely shocked that they had been cooperating with the
investigation and had offered to surrender her voluntarily if she was charged.
A reporter asked state attorney Catherine Fernandez Rundle why they had not let her turn herself in.
Rundle said the circumstances were a little more unusual, that Clennie was far away on a
remote island and that the right thing was to go and get her and secure her presence.
That afternoon, she appeared before a judge in Hilo and waved extradition.
Her public defender there asked the judge to keep cameras out, arguing that the international
attention could hurt her chance at a fair trial. The judge allowed the cameras.
A prosecutor told the court she also had outstanding warrants in Nevada and Texas.
The judge held her without bail. Rundle, at her own news conference in Miami that morning,
said the violent and toxic two-year relationship of Christian Obumseli and Courtney Clennie
did not have to end in tragedy, with Christian's murder as a victim of domestic violence.
The warrant's own conclusion was that the two had been in a violent and toxic
domestic relationship for over two years, which often escalated into Clennie throwing
or using weapons, and that on April 3 she acted without justification in an
imminently dangerous act demonstrating a depraved mind without regard for human life.
Clennie was extradited to Florida and held without bond. Prosecutors argued her social

Knight Correctional Center and she pleaded not guilty. She would stay in that jail for four years,
a county jail, not a prison, held without bond while both sides fought over depositions.
That is worth knowing when you hear that her sentence is six years and she has about two left.
Nearly all of the first four were served before anyone had decided she was guilty of anything.
Now I want to give the defense its due because a plea deal does not mean the defense had nothing.
Frank Piedos said the arrest warrant contained deceptive and incomplete statements.
He said it was a shame the state attorney's office was trying to win the case in the
court of public opinion by showing what he called an irrelevant and likely inadmissible elevator video.
His point about that video was that it does not show what happened before it started.
His position on Obamselli was blunt. Obamselli was the abuser, he said,
the worst kind of abuser who would manipulate and abuse Courtney and Pry that when he thought

of domestic abuse who survived her abuser. Court filing showed that at trial the defense

grabbed, shoved, restrained and choked her. Some of it was specific. An April 2021 text in

A trip to Dubai where she says an argument about marijuana ended with him shoving her
hard enough that she believed she had fractured her ribs and she did not get it looked at.
An incident in Austin in January 2022 that she says left her with an injured finger.
Here is where I have to be careful and so should you. Those are allegations in a court filing.
They were never tested in front of a jury and the man they accused has been dead since 2022 and
cannot answer them. Both sides also pointed at that same Aspen video, the one from a trip
weeks before his death where she is screaming at him and hitting him and each side said it
proved their client was the one being abused. That tells you something about how this case

It was set for trial at the end of April 2026 then pushed when both sides filed a joint motion.
Prosecutors had 15 or 16 depositions scheduled and witnesses were not showing up,

She asked, if we're in the same position next time we come back and these witnesses are just
not appearing there's going to come a time when it's fish or cut bait right? There was a

They sued Clenny for battery and they also sued the condominium association,
the property manager and the security companies arguing the building failed to provide

The family's position was that with all of that on the record what happened in 2201 was foreseeable

Ten days after that last civil order on July 31, 2026,
Clenny's lawyer told TMZ she had reached a plea deal. Civil case closed first,
criminal case second. Lawyers do it in that order on purpose so statements from one
proceeding cannot be used against a defendant in the other. Her lawyers confirmed there was a deal

She reserved the right to challenge that. The family was in the room.
Obumselli's mother, Cio, read a statement.
There is simply too much pain to put on paper, she said. Four years later there are still
nights when I cannot sleep. I do not want Christian to be remembered only for how he died.

Words can never fully explain, she said, how Christian's death has affected my life and the

Your actions have left the Obumselli family with a void that can never be filled, they said.
A chair where a family gathers for holidays will always remain empty. His life had meaning.
He had a future and his family deserved to grow with him. He was robbed of all those things
while you still have all yours to enjoy. The family also told the court something that
has stayed with me. They said he had stayed in a relationship they called destructive,
despite previous violence, that he had been cut in the face and stabbed before,
and that he had written about his fear that his love for Courtney Clenny could cost him his life.
So what does this actually resolve, less than a verdict would have? State Attorney
Fernandez Rundle said the family finally heard what they had long sought, Courtney

focused on the core evidence that Clenny stabbed him as part of a pattern of escalating violence

justice too long denied. The family's attorney said pleading guilty and accepting full responsibility
would begin the process of bringing closure. That is real. An admission in open court from
her own mouth is something the family did not have for four years. But a plea also
closes the door on the questions. No jury ever weighed the battered spouse case. No jury ever
heard the elevator video next to those text messages and decided what the relationship actually was.
Pomeroy was right, and it cut both ways. The state faced a self-defense claim and
depositions that would not happen, and the defense faced a medical examiner and a video.
What the record leaves us with is this. Two people in a relationship that everyone around
them described as violent and toxic. Documented violence by her, on camera, more than once.
Serious allegations against him that never got tested. A man who died on an April afternoon in
his own apartment 25 minutes after walking in with sandwiches. And a plea four years to the day after
the arrest that ends the case without ever answering it. Christiano Boomseli was 27.
If anything here sounds familiar to you, the National Domestic Violence Hotline is
